summary:
Uzbekistan’s textile and apparel exports rose 28.1 per cent to $2.4 billion in January–September 2026, with finished products at 50.8 per cent.
Russia remains the key outlet, taking about 62 per cent in January–October 2025 and most knitted apparel and home textiles.
Domestic processing and yarn levies are tightening Uzbek cotton yarn supply for spinners in Türkiye, China and Bangladesh.

title: Weak yarn demand meets steady costs: Where will VSF go?
summary:
China’s viscose staple fibre quotes edged up over October 23 to November 2, 2026, with 1.2D and 1.5D ending near $2.21/kg on November 2.
All four domestic grades closed higher: 1.2D and 1.5D rose 0.2 per cent, high-end fibre gained 0.4 per cent and medium grade led with 0.7 per cent.
Stable chemical inputs and slim textile buying kept the upward move cautious, with momentum already flattening.

title: EU rules by 2028: Will Asia capture the textile-recycling opportunity?
summary:
US recycler Circ and China’s Huafon have announced a textile-to-textile recycling plant in China to process about 200 tonnes of blended polyester-cotton waste a day.
The plant will recover PTA, MEG and cellulose pulp, signalling capacity moving closer to Asian polyester and garment production.
Europe’s rules create waste-handling costs from 2028, but do not compel recycled-fibre purchases.

title: India targets $1 trn in exports after record $863 bn last year: Goyal
summary:
India's exports rose 14 per cent year on year to $480 billion in April-September, putting the country on track towards its $1 trillion annual target, which requires another $520 billion in the second half. 
India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the IMF had revised its global trade growth forecast to around 3.5 per cent, with India's export performance potentially contributing to the increase.

title: South Indian cotton yarn prices ease amid weak demand, duty relief
summary:
South Indian cotton yarn weakened after duty-free cotton imports were extended until December, with Mumbai prices down ₹2–3 (~$0.02–0.03) per kg amid weak demand, tight liquidity and profit-booking.
Tiruppur stayed steady as mills rolled over November rates but offered discounts to attract buyers ahead of Diwali.
Gujarat cotton fell ₹1,500–1,800 per candy as mill demand slowed and new-crop arrivals rose.

title: Can China power North Africa’s textile rise? Egypt’s $2.9 bn test
summary:
EU-27 imports of Egyptian knitted and woven apparel reached $747 million in January-June 2026, up 29.1 per cent year on year, against the bloc’s 3.6 per cent apparel import growth.
Egypt’s garment exports hit $3.394 billion in 2025, but spinning and textile imports exceeded exports by $2.864 billion.
Chinese-backed projects in Egypt and Morocco target yarn, fabric, dyeing and finishing capacity.

title: Techtextil and Texprocess 2028 strengthen textile value-chain links
summary:
Techtextil and Texprocess will return to Frankfurt on 4–7 April 2028 with an optimised hall layout linking materials, production technologies and processing.
Leading exhibitors have already registered, including Lenzing, Toray Textiles Europe, Kornit and Veit.
The concurrent fairs aim to strengthen value-chain collaboration, with early-booking rates available until 30 November 2026.

title: China's central bank adopts overnight reverse repo as main policy rate
summary:
China's central bank shifted its main policy rate anchor from the seven-day to the overnight reverse repo rate on November 2, conducting 541 billion yuan ($81.1 billion) of overnight operations at 1.25 per cent. 
Under the revised framework, overnight reverse repos will become the PBOC's primary open-market instrument, with other related rates also linked to the new benchmark.

title: India's manufacturing PMI eases to 54.7 in October: S&P Global
summary:
India’s manufacturing PMI fell to 54.7 in October from 55.1 in September but stayed above the 50.0 neutral mark and its long-run average.
New export orders grew at the fastest rate in six months, supporting output even as overall new business and production growth softened.
Input cost inflation fell to its lowest since February, while hiring rose only slightly and confidence weakened.

title: Functional Fabric Fair Fall 2026 sets attendance record in Portland
summary:
Functional Fabric Fair’s Fall 2026 edition in Portland drew record attendance, up 7 per cent, with over 350 exhibitors and a sold-out Day 0 OIA Catalyst Conference.
Held on 26–28 October, the event highlighted bio-based materials, sustainable sourcing and performance textiles through expert talks, innovation forums and awards, connecting brands with suppliers and emerging technologies.

title: 600 fewer units, $1 bn down. India’s apparel crisis exposed
summary:
US apparel imports from India fell 25.96 per cent to $2.891 billion in January–August 2026, far outpacing the overall US market's 7.02 per cent contraction.
India's share slipped to 5.59 per cent, with $740 million of the decline tied to lost share, TexPro analysis shows.
Noida industry estimates point to 600 fewer operating units and weaker exports.

title: Bangladesh's exports rise 6% to $17.04 bn in Jul-Oct, led by RMG
summary:
Bangladesh's merchandise exports rose nearly 6.0 per cent year on year to $17.04 billion in July-October of FY27, led by readymade garments, Bangladesh Bank data showed.
Knitwear exports grew 7.0 per cent to $7.71 billion, while woven garments rose 4.80 per cent to $6.0 billion.
Jute goods, leather goods, home textiles and footwear also increased, but cotton products declined 10.2 per cent.

title: AmCham urges Bangladesh to boost productivity, diversify exports
summary:
AmCham Bangladesh president Syed Mohammad Kamal has urged the country to use its LDC graduation deferment to November 24, 2029, to raise productivity and diversify exports.
He said about 73 per cent of merchandise exports use LDC-specific preferences, while readymade garments made up 81 per cent in FY2025-26.
He also sought GSP+ preparation and a time-bound Smooth Transition Strategy.

title: Why Sri Lanka’s proposed anti-terror Bill has trade bodies worried
summary:
Sri Lankan business bodies have raised concerns over the proposed terrorism bill’s impact on investor confidence, legal certainty and EU GSP+ access.
The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce and JAAF seek clearer safeguards as apparel exporters face reapplication under the EU’s 2027 framework.
Textile and apparel exports exceeded $5 billion in 2025, with the EU taking 31.3 per cent.

title: Bangladesh forms wage board to review garment workers' pay
summary:
Bangladesh formed a six-member wage board to review garment workers’ minimum pay amid protests demanding Tk 30,000 (~$240) per month. 
The panel, comprising employer, worker and independent representatives, will recommend a revised wage structure. 
The current minimum wage is Tk 12,500, while recent labour law amendments reduced the wage review cycle from five years to three.

title: AAFA urges USTR to avoid reinstating China-linked maritime fees
summary:
AAFA backed extending the suspension of US maritime fees on China-linked shipping until January 9, 2027, but urged USTR to seek a longer-term solution. 
It warned that reinstating fees and equipment tariffs could raise costs and disrupt supply chains, calling for investment and allied partnerships to strengthen US maritime capacity.

title: Indian exporters gearing up for a bigger European play?

Gokaldas Exports sees Europe’s export share rising to 25–30 per cent in three to five years, while Raymond Lifestyle targets 20–25 per cent.
EU sustainability and traceability rules will shape lasting gains.

title: How can Bangladesh apparel exporters reduce payment risks?
summary:

The cases underline the need for due diligence, clear contracts and bank-backed, lawful payment safeguards.

title: Turkiye’s apparel exports decline 2.2% in first three quarters

Subdued European demand, cautious buying and price competition continue to pressure exporters.

title: Bangladesh’s EU apparel market: A changing export landscape?
summary:

Spain overtook Germany in Q1 FY2026–27, with shipments up 13.73 per cent to $1.148 billion against Germany’s $1.123 billion.
Volumes fell 4.58 per cent and unit prices 7.43 per cent, while China and Vietnam gained ground ahead of Bangladesh’s LDC graduation.
